verdict.rationale: Gitleaks natively scans entire directories or full git histories in one invocation (e.g. `gitleaks dir path`, `gitleaks git <dir>` scanning multiple commits/files and returning aggregated JSON reports), and gitleaks-action can run bulk scans across all PRs/commits in a CI workflow — this is genuine bulk operation over many items in a single run. However there's no evidence of an AI-agent-oriented bulk API, batch job orchestration across multiple repos/orgs at once, or programmatic control tailored to agentic bulk workflows. Missing for 10: multi-repo/organization-wide batch scanning in one command, a machine-callable bulk API (llms.txt/OpenAPI probes both 404), and any AI-native orchestration layer beyond standard CLI/CI usage.
